items.note: Bhāillasvāmippura is the ancient city of Vidishā (Bhilsā), formerly capital of the Akara-janapada, roughly east Mālava; named from a Sun image, with Albērūnī (c. 1030 A.C.) quoted.
Earliest mention of the name Bhillasvāmin is in an inscription of V.S. 935 or 878 A.C.; also Bhillasvāmipura in the Māndhātā inscription of V.S. 1331.
Vētravatī is the river Bēwā flowing by the city of Bhilsā.

items.note: Udayavarman's grant (V.S. 1256) lists Yasōvarman, Jayavarman, Lakshmīvarman, Harischandra and Udayavarman; Lakshmīvarman established himself in the Bhopāl region as subordinate to the Imperial Paramāra house.
Mahākumāra house held the Mahādvādaśaka region to 1157 A.C.; it then passed to Chaulukya Kumārapāla per an inscription of V.S. 1220 and an Ajayapāla inscription 'at Udaipur' of V.S. 1229.
Jayavarman's son Vindhyavarman recovered ancestral dominions from Chaulukya Mūlarāja II, after the present grant, and had to fight the Yādavas and Hoysalas.
